content.text: I have written a sample utility for this. I have tested it with the default leveldb cachestore as well as with a postgres-based JDBC cachestore.
https://github.com/acoburn/fcrepo-namespace-util
That said, I don't actually have any unit tests for this at present.
The
fcrepo-namespace-util
project would be a great addition to -labs and eventually -exts. What would you like to happen now, however?
Actually, it already is in -labs:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-namespace-util
I think the question is: does this utility address the ticket?
, does this utility address the ticket?
, I am going to take a look at it today.
Based on IRC feedback, this utility as it currently stands has the potential to render a Fedora installation unusable.
See:
http://irclogs.fcrepo.org/2016-05-20.html
– starting at 16:39
I have been unable to reproduce the error I encountered last Friday (5/20). I did notice a couple of other things:

Attempting to change an existing prefix to another namespace appears to succeed in the tool, but after restarting the repository, then re-running the tool, the original prefix is restored to its original URI, and the other namespace URI disappears from the list of prefixes.
There is a
ns00X
prefix with the URI
http://www.w3.org/ns/auth/acl#accessControl:

that cannot be changed, because it is part of a node type definition. That is an odd-looking URI to be a prefix from a pure RDF standpoint, so I was wondering if this is an expected prefix or something that has gotten screwed up on our local installation.
Just as a clarifying point – when you ran the namespace-changing utility, was the repository stopped? (It is expected that the repository be stopped)
Yes, the repository was stopped before running namespace-util.
I modified the code so that any namespace registered as a
nodetype
is filtered out of the list and so a user can't even attempt to change those values (as opposed to the earlier, naive approach – just try to change everything but catch exceptions).
, to follow up on (1) from my comment above, I have noticed further behavior. In my original test, I re-assigned the
dc
prefix from
http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/
to
http://purl.org/dc/terms/
(the latter was showing up with a
ns00X

prefix, although I currently had no objects using any properties in that namespace). The tool accepted the changes, and Fedora started up alright, but when I shut down Fedora and restarted the tool, the `dc` namespace had reverted to
http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/
But now when I try to add a property in the
http://purl.org/dc/terms/
namespace, I keep getting a "Not Implemented" error. This happens both when I try using the full URI in the predicate position of if I define a prefix in the SPARQL update.
INSERT { <> <http://purl.org/dc/terms/title> "Foobar" }

PREFIX dcterms: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/>
INSERT { <> dcterms:title "Foobar" }
I suspect the namespaces defined in the CND file may complicate the use of this utility, as seen in the case of:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-kernel-modeshape/src/main/resources/fedora-node-types.cnd#L19
To prevent unpleasant interactions with the CND file, would it help to define a blacklist of namespaces/prefixes not to touch?
Yes, a blacklist with those values from the CND would be a good idea – I'll add that now
I am inclined to deep-6 the namespace changing tool I wrote earlier, and instead recommend that users define namespaces in a custom CND file. Do you have any objections to closing this ticket?
Fine by me. Custom CND sounds like a better option.

Closing this as a back-end utility appears not to be the best way to approach this. Instead, a recommendation to use a custom CND file with the defined namespace prefixes seems to be a better approach.
This task is to create a backend utility that allows Fedora administrators to provide preferred namespace prefixes that will then override existing prefix mappings in the repository.
As a part of this task or a follow-on documentation ticket, this utility should be documented in the wiki.
See:
https://groups.google.com/d/msg/fedora-tech/1F0paNOp9GY/lUHI9niwOpQJ
